title: Cloud migration of an enterprise data analytics platform
description: 12-month, $1.2M migration of ~200 servers from 6 legacy data centers to AWS — zero unscheduled downtime, delivered within fixed budget and timeline.
overview: A pilot cloud migration for a global financial services enterprise: ~200 servers behind its internal data analytics platform, spread across six aging data centers, moved to AWS in 12 months on a $1.2M fixed budget with zero unscheduled downtime. The pilot had to prove AWS feasibility and produce the SOPs, architecture decision records and validated patterns for the larger enterprise modernization to follow.
highlights: Sequenced the lift-and-shift as ten prioritized use cases, each migrated end to end inside a two-week sprint
Ran every use case through the same five-step cycle (Discover → Move → Rebuild → Validate → Cutover), with UAT as a mandatory quality gate before any production cutover
Planned a 12-month Gantt with Use Case 1 as an extended pathfinder, later use cases in parallel pairs, and a hypercare close-out
Held a fixed-rate, fixed-FTE budget envelope and a risk register of four domains, each with mitigations, owners and a measurable success state
Delivered the SOPs, architecture decision records and pattern library the enterprise uses to scale the same approach
technicalApproach: Each use case moved through Discover (dependency analysis, scope confirmation), Move (data sources to the AWS target), Rebuild (processing and application logic), Validate (web server plus end-to-end UAT) and Cutover (formal cutover and resource retirement). A two-tier governance model with defined ceremonies and escalation paths kept delivery focused.
ogLine: 12 months · $1.2M fixed budget · zero unscheduled downtime
caption: One square per server — before and after.
alt: Figure: six legacy data centers, about 200 servers in total, consolidated into one AWS environment.

title: Data warehouse modernization program
description: 18-month fixed-fee program migrating a legacy SQL Server data warehouse to Snowflake, dbt, and Tableau — governed by formal change control, contractual gateways, and three-tier stakeholder management.
overview: A multi-project program migrating a US FinTech enterprise's legacy SQL Server data warehouse to Snowflake, dbt and Tableau. It was designed around three non-negotiables: a fixed 18-month term, fixed consultancy fees and zero scope drift, defended by formal gateways, a parking-lot system and an explicit change-control process.
highlights: Structured the program as three phases (Initiation, Delivery, Closure), each ending at a contractual gateway
Routed every scope addition through a three-step Change Control Process (Route → Quantify → Decide) so the fixed fee was never absorbed silently
Ran a four-step way-of-working (Development → Presentation → Formal Agreement → Execution & Review), signed off by the client PM
Reported four KPIs to the C-level: cost variance under 5%, 100% milestone completion, data validation above 98% and change-request frequency
Kept a centralised RAID log and a three-tier stakeholder model with defined cadence and escalation criteria
technicalApproach: Initiation mapped data sources and dependencies to fix the contract boundary. Delivery opened with a PoC to validate the approach and refine estimates, then iterated in agile cycles with mandatory UAT by the client's data analysts gating every release. Closure confirmed adherence to the fixed mandate and decommissioned the legacy warehouse.
ogLine: 18 months · fixed fee · three-tier stakeholder model
caption: Program shape and contractual gateways (illustrative).
alt: Figure: 18-month program plan. Discovery, Snowflake, dbt models, Tableau and cutover workstreams across four contractual gateways.

title: Data intelligence platform build
description: A 12-month engagement to take a mid-market trading company from scattered operational systems to a unified data platform — Data Lake, Data Warehouse, BI, and predictive models, built from scratch with a hybrid agile planning model.
overview: A 12-month engagement that took a mid-market trading company from three disconnected operational systems to a unified data platform: data lake, data warehouse, BI and predictive models, built from scratch. A high-level annual plan locked the macro phases and milestones, with two-week sprints executing inside each phase.
highlights: Planned the year as four quarterly milestones a non-technical sponsor could verify: data in the raw layer, BI MVP delivered, predictive solution shipped, opportunities report delivered
Introduced a three-level backlog (Deliverable → Activity → Task) that maps the contract, the team conversation and the sprint
Ran Sprint 1 without slack as a calibration exercise, then fed measured capacity into Sprint 2 onwards
Closed the year with the team trained, an expansion roadmap delivered and two new features contracted
technicalApproach: Hybrid planning: an annual plan of four phases (Planning, MVP execution, Deploy & test, Monitor & report) with Scrum sprints and a Kanban workflow inside each. Q1 produced the diagnostic report, system specification and first data lake ingestion, each with its own acceptance criteria.
ogLine: 12 months · 3 systems unified · every milestone on time
caption: The platform, layer by layer, quarter by quarter.
alt: Figure: a data platform built over four quarters — data lake, then warehouse, BI layer and predictive models stacked on top.

title: Spotify ELT pipeline with AWS, Airflow and dbt
description: End-to-end ELT data lake pulling Spotify's global playlist data through a 4-stage medallion architecture on AWS S3, orchestrated by Airflow and transformed with dbt — delivered to Power BI dashboards.
overview: A cost-effective data lake built on the "poor man's data lake" concept — DuckDB, Motherduck, dbt, and Airflow processing data from the Spotify API. The pipeline extracts tracks, albums, and artists from popular global playlists and moves them through four sequential stages (Raw → Bronze → Silver → Gold), storing each as Parquet files in AWS S3. Airflow on Astronomer orchestrates daily batch runs; dbt handles all transformations with automated testing and documentation; Terraform provisions the S3 infrastructure; and Power BI surfaces the final analytics layer.
highlights: Designed a 4-stage medallion architecture (Raw/Bronze/Silver/Gold) using DuckDB and AWS S3, keeping infrastructure costs near zero
Orchestrated daily Spotify API extraction via Astronomer and Airflow with modular, testable task groups
Provisioned S3 buckets and external Motherduck tables with Terraform for reproducible, code-driven infrastructure
Transformed data through dbt-core with automated testing and documentation, deployed to both dev and prod environments
Delivered analytics-ready Power BI dashboards covering playlist trends, artist reach, and track-level metrics
technicalApproach: Raw stage ingests JSON from the Spotify API into S3. Bronze converts raw JSON to Parquet via DuckDB. Silver applies business-rule cleaning and enrichment. Gold runs dbt models to produce analytics-ready dimensional tables in Motherduck, which Power BI queries directly.
caption: Each stage narrower, cleaner, closer to a decision.
alt: Figure: Spotify API data moving through raw, bronze, silver and gold stages into Power BI.

title: Adventure Works data pipeline with dbt and BigQuery
description: Analytics engineering certification project — a three-layer dbt pipeline (staging, intermediate, marts) transforming 64 SAP source tables into analytics-ready dimensional models on BigQuery.
overview: Built as part of the Analytics Engineer certification from Indicium Academy, this project ingests and transforms Adventure Works SAP data using dbt Core and BigQuery. Sixty-four source tables flow through three layers: staging standardizes and cleans raw inputs, intermediate applies transformation logic and prepares join-ready datasets, and marts deliver business-facing dimensional models organized by domain. Each layer is covered by automated dbt tests and generated documentation.
highlights: Modeled 64 SAP source tables into a clean dimensional schema using dbt Core's three-layer architecture on BigQuery
Wrote automated dbt tests (not-null, unique, accepted-values) and generated docs across every model layer
Designed mart-layer models organized by business subject, directly consumable by BI tools
technicalApproach: Staging layer handles raw data standardization and type casting. Intermediate layer applies transformation logic and prepares datasets for joining. Marts layer delivers final dimensional models organized by business subject area.
ogLine: 64 SAP tables · 3 dbt layers · every layer tested
caption: From source sprawl to a dimensional model.
alt: Figure: 64 SAP source tables reduced to one star schema through staging, intermediate and mart layers.

title: E-commerce ETL pipeline with BigQuery and DuckDB
description: Python ETL pipeline that extracts e-commerce data from BigQuery public datasets, validates it with Pydantic, loads it into DuckDB, and sinks to multiple destinations — local CSV, Amazon S3, and MotherDuck.
overview: A modular Python ETL pipeline built around the BigQuery public dataset 'thelook_ecommerce'. Data is extracted from BigQuery, validated for type safety and business rules using Pydantic models, loaded into DuckDB for efficient in-process analysis, and then sinked to one of three configurable destinations: local CSV files, Amazon S3, or MotherDuck. The pipeline is composed of independent, testable components for BigQuery interactions, DuckDB operations, and data validation.
highlights: Extracted and validated e-commerce data from BigQuery using Pydantic models to enforce schema and type safety at ingestion
Loaded validated data into DuckDB for fast, in-process analytical queries without standing up a separate database server
Built a flexible multi-destination sink layer supporting local CSV, Amazon S3, and MotherDuck based on runtime configuration
Structured the pipeline as modular Python components — BigQuery extractor, DuckDB loader, Pydantic validator, and sink adapters — for independent testing and reuse
technicalApproach: Extract from BigQuery using table names as input, validate records with Pydantic models, load into DuckDB for processing, then sink to the configured destination (CSV, S3, or MotherDuck) based on runtime parameters.
ogLine: 3 runtime sinks · 4 testable modules · typed ingestion
caption: Typed at the gate, routed by configuration.
alt: Figure: BigQuery rows validated by Pydantic, loaded into DuckDB, then routed to CSV, S3 or MotherDuck.
